stem: The data produced by a certain data entry firm always include a small number of incorrect characters that occur at random. The proportion of incorrect characters is denoted by $p$, and experience has shown that $p = 0.0001$. A particular data set from the firm contains $14\,500$ characters, of which $X$ characters are incorrect.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use a suitable approximating distribution to find $\text{P}(X < 4)$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The firm’s management wishes to decrease the value of $p$ by giving their employees some training. Their aim is that, for a data set containing $14\,500$ characters, the value of $\text{P}(X = 0)$ for the new value of $p$ should be double the value of $\text{P}(X = 0)$ when $p = 0.0001$.
parts.text: Use a suitable approximating distribution to find the new value of $p$.
